entity.name: Nikhil Bharti
entity.description: I am a final-year B.Tech CSE student in Himachal Pradesh, India, building open-source bioinformatics tools that run locally on low-cost hardware. I started Genomic Equity Conformal after noticing that many genetic variant models are calibrated mostly on European datasets and require cloud uploads that smaller Indian labs cannot easily use.

projects.name: Genomic Equity Conformal
projects.description: An open-source, local-first quality-assurance sidecar for clinical variant interpretation pipelines (MIT code, CC BY 4.0 data). Version 5.0.0 indexes all 19,276 HGNC human protein-coding genes and 67,402 ClinVar GRCh38 missense variants (2-star and above) into a single 15.75 MB offline SQLite file. Using 7-ancestry Mondrian conformal calibration, it cuts expected calibration error by 90.4% across South Asian, African, East Asian, Admixed American, Middle Eastern, European, and founder cohorts, while running on a standard CPU in about 1.46 seconds at ~185 MB RAM. Strictly a research and pipeline QA sidecar, not a standalone medical diagnostic device.
